components.name: Timbre
components.description: 88px round red contact submit with a steel ring; presses and turns bright while sending.
components.css: .ds-timbre { position: relative; flex-shrink: 0; width: 88px; height: 88px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 40%, #e5e9f2, #7d879c); box-shadow: 0 8px 18px -6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6), inset 0 -3px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25); cursor: pointer; } .ds-timbre-cap { position: absolute; inset: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 40% 32%, #ff6a5c, #c8261a 60%, #8a140c); box-shadow: 0 5px 0 #6d0f08, 0 8px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35); transition: transform 100ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 100ms, background 200ms; } .ds-timbre:hover .ds-timbre-cap { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-timbre:active .ds-timbre-cap, .ds-timbre[data-pressed] .ds-timbre-cap { transform: translateY(4px); } .ds-timbre[data-pressed] .ds-timbre-cap { background: radial-gradient(circle at 40% 32%, #ffd0c9, #ff3b2a 55%, #b21c10); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #6d0f08, 0 0 28px 6px rgba(255, 59, 42, 0.55); } .ds-timbre:disabled { cursor: progress; } .ds-timbre:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffb000; outline-offset: 5px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-sr { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
The page is a Buenos Aires colectivo route. The navy ground is the bus livery, and each section is a stop along the line: Inicio, Skills, Proyectos, Contacto. The header carries the route itself, a four-stop line with a bus that moves along it on damped spring physics. The LED destination sign in the hero is the memorable first moment, drawn in amber dot-matrix on canvas. Projects are printed boletos on paper stock, and contact is the round red timbre you press to get off.

The personality is friendly and plain-spoken, in Spanish with rioplatense ease. Density is generous: one stop fills most of a viewport, and projects are full-bleed livery bands rather than cards in a grid. The world is literal on purpose. Objects that exist on a bus (the sign housing, the ticket machine, the window, the paper ticket, the bell) carry physical depth. Surfaces that are only print (livery bands, text) stay flat.
keyCharacteristics: Navy livery ground with full-bleed colour bands per section and per project.
Amber dot-matrix LED sign, rendered in canvas from src/scripts/led.ts.
Paper boletos with perforated top and bottom edges.
Round red timbre as the contact submit; notched amber ticket as the primary action.
Header route line with four stops and a spring-driven bus.
Big Shoulders Display for headings and labels over Archivo Variable for body.

rules.name: The Livery Rule
rules.body: Every section and every project is a full-bleed band of one livery colour. Navy carries the page, yellow is the skills stop, red is the contact stop, and the project bands cycle the five livery colours in order.

rules.name: The Route Colour Rule
rules.body: Amber is the one signal colour. It marks the current stop, the bus, the LED characters and the primary action. Its rarity on text is the point.

rules.name: The Destination Caps Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are set in Big Shoulders Display, uppercase, and never in a system display face. Body copy stays in Archivo Variable in sentence case.

rules.name: The Physical Object Rule
rules.body: Only objects that exist in the bus carry depth. Shadows are large and soft, and they never appear on livery bands or on text.

dos: Do set every section on a full-bleed livery band, cycling the project colours in order blue, red, amber, green, violet.
Do keep amber as the single signal colour for current state, the bus, the LED and the primary action.
Do make primary actions physical: the notched ticket for the CV and the round red timbre for contact.
Do keep print surfaces (boletos, windows) on the paper and navy stock, with perforated or framed edges.
Do use the 1180px container and --gutter for all content width.
donts: Don't set body or heading text in Archivo or Big Shoulders in a light or pale colour on yellow or amber; navy is the ink on those grounds.
Don't introduce a hue outside the palette above.
Don't replace the perforated boleto, the notched ticket or the round timbre with flat rectangles; those shapes are the identity.
Don't set headings in a system display face.
Don't copy the hard offset shadows on the timbre cap or the skills plate. They are build defects, not the system.
Don't put a shadow on a livery band or on text.
